reasons.plausibility: Friction-induced oxide formation as a protective tribo-layer is supported by established tribology principles, making the mechanism consistent with known high-temperature alloy behavior.
reasons.testability: Comparing wear and friction in oxidizing vs. inert atmospheres, alongside direct oxide characterization, provides a clear, decisive experiment to confirm or refute the role of oxide scale formation.
reasons.usefulness: Confirming whether a self-lubricating oxide tribo-layer governs wear performance directly informs coating design and optimization for high-entropy alloys in demanding applications.
